selection_description: One skill selection for a Unitree G1 humanoid with {n_joints} joints. The host plans the skill, checks it against joint and speed limits, runs it to its end (arm_sdk joint targets; LocoClient velocity commands for the base; the onboard controller for gestures), waits for the joints to settle, then supplies a fresh observation with the result.

note.description: 1-2 short sentences: the current visual evidence and the purpose of this action.

skills.name: move
skills.description: One relative base displacement: dx_m forward, dy_m left (sidestep) and dyaw_deg turn, in the frame the robot stands in now. Translates first, then turns.
skills.prompt: Move the base by dx_m forward (-3 to 3; negative walks backward), dy_m left (-1.5 to 1.5; a sidestep) and dyaw_deg (-180 to 180, positive turns LEFT), in the current frame. The host translates at 0.2 m/s then turns at 0.4 rad/s, observing every 3 s but not re-deciding. Only when the note states the floor is clear for the whole displacement; a 1 m move takes 5 s. To face a visible target, turn by its bearing (the image spans about 77 degrees horizontally). To search, turn LEFT in steps of 45-60 degrees and observe between turns; after a full circle without seeing the goal, move 0.5 m into clear space and search again. To pass an obstacle, sidestep or turn around it in short moves rather than walking at it.

skills.name: arm_path
skills.description: Move the waist and arms through joint-space waypoints: each waypoint names joints and their target angles in radians and how long to take; omitted joints keep their pose.
skills.prompt: Move the waist and arms through 1 to 8 joint-space waypoints; each gives joints (name -> radians, see the joint table) and seconds (0.5 to 10, default 2). Omitted joints keep their current pose. Use waist_yaw alone (positive LEFT, up to +/-45 degrees = 0.785 rad) to glance sideways without moving the feet; the next arm_path or move may recentre it. Keep the arms clear of the body and the head; the host rejects a path that leaves the joint limits or moves too fast, without moving. A gesture, a glance or a reach: not a search move.

skills.name: hold
skills.description: Stand still for seconds, keeping the current pose and waist direction.
skills.prompt: Stand still for seconds (0.1 to 30, default 1) keeping the current pose. Use it to wait for a moving obstacle or a person to clear, or to observe again without moving.

skills.name: check
skills.description: Dry-run a skill with the given arguments from the current commanded pose without moving: joint limits, command speed, base velocity limits, duration and the resulting base displacement. No physics or contact check.
skills.prompt: Check a skill and its arguments without moving: the host plans it from the current commanded pose and reports joint-limit, command-speed and base-velocity violations, its duration and the base displacement it would produce. It does not simulate contact or prove the path is clear; judge that from the image. Use it for an uncertain long move or an arm_path near the limits before committing; every movement is dry-run this way before it executes anyway.

arguments.description: the arguments that skill would run with (its note may be omitted)

skills.name: wave_hand
skills.description: The robot's own wave gesture (onboard controller): it takes the arms for the gesture and hands them back. Robot only.
skills.prompt: Wave with the onboard controller's built-in gesture; turn_flag true adds a turn of the hand. The host hands the arms to the onboard controller for seconds (default 4), then takes them back. A greeting toward a person; not a search move.

turn_flag.description: wave with a turn of the hand

seconds.description: how long the onboard gesture takes

skills.name: shake_hand
skills.description: The robot's own handshake gesture (onboard controller). Robot only.
skills.prompt: Offer a handshake with the onboard controller's built-in gesture (stage -1 runs the whole gesture). The host hands the arms to the onboard controller for seconds (default 6), then takes them back. Only when a person stands within reach in front of the robot.

seconds.description: how long the onboard gesture takes

skills.name: done
skills.description: Request task completion only when fresh observations establish the outcome. This is the model's conclusion; a human assigns the final success/failure label after the run.
skills.prompt: End the task only when the current image establishes the goal: for a search, the goal object is clearly visible and near (large, or in the lower third of the image). done is not a success label; a human assigns that after the run. In summary, give the direct evidence and any remaining uncertainty; in hindsight, what would have made this run shorter or surer.

summary.description: direct current evidence of the requested outcome and any remaining uncertainty

skills.name: give_up
skills.description: End the task when it cannot be completed.
skills.prompt: End when evidence shows the task cannot be completed safely within the decision budget. One failed action, blocked path or unseen goal does not establish impossibility: search from another spot first. In reason, list the strategies tried and the evidence that no reasonable safe continuation remains; hindsight records lessons from this attempt.

skills.name: walk_forward
skills.description: Walk straight ahead by distance_m metres at 0.2 m/s, then stand still.
skills.prompt: Walk straight ahead by distance_m metres (0.1 to 3.0) at 0.2 m/s; a 3 m walk takes 15 s and is observed every 3 s but not re-decided. Only when the note states that the floor ahead is clear for that distance. The head camera looks 47 degrees down, so the floor 1-3 m ahead fills the lower half of the image. Walk when the goal is centred and far; turn first when it is off-centre.

skills.name: turn
skills.description: Turn in place by angle_deg degrees at 0.4 rad/s: positive = LEFT (counter-clockwise), negative = RIGHT.
skills.prompt: Turn in place by angle_deg degrees (-180 to 180); positive turns LEFT, negative RIGHT. To face a visible goal, turn by its bearing (the image spans about 77 degrees horizontally). To search, turn LEFT in steps of 45-60 degrees and observe between turns; after a full circle without seeing the goal, walk 0.5 m into clear space and search again.

skills.name: look
skills.description: Turn only the waist (not the feet) by yaw_deg and hold it, so the next image looks sideways: positive = LEFT, negative = RIGHT. The next skill recentres the waist.
skills.prompt: Turn only the waist by yaw_deg degrees (-45 to 45), positive LEFT, and hold it so the next image looks sideways; the feet do not move and the next skill recentres the waist. Use it to glance around when turning is not offered, or to inspect something beside the robot.

skills.name: tpose
skills.description: Raise both arms straight out to the sides (a T-pose), hold, then lower them.
skills.prompt: Raise both arms straight out to the sides, hold for hold seconds, then lower them (rise seconds each way). A gesture, not a search move; needs clear space to both sides at shoulder height.

skills.name: sixseven
skills.description: A two-handed see-saw wave: palms up, forearms swing up and down in turn, then arms down.
skills.prompt: A two-handed see-saw wave with the palms up: reps swings per hand of swing_time seconds each, after settle seconds to reach the palms-up pose and hold seconds before and after. A gesture toward a person; not a search move.

settle.description: seconds to reach the palms-up pose

hold.description: seconds to hold before and after

skills.name: takeover
skills.description: Bookend: ramp the arm_sdk weight 0 to 1 while holding the pose observed at reset, then go to STAND.

skills.name: handback
skills.description: Bookend: go to STAND, then hold it while ramping the weight 1 to 0 so the onboard controller takes the arms back smoothly.
